name: window-management-plus
title: Window Management+
description: Companion to Raycast's Window Management, inspired by Hyprland. Tile every open window at once with master and grid layouts, swap, rotate, and move windows between displays. Requires Raycast Pro.
author: connorforsyth

preferences.name: screenGap
preferences.title: Screen Gap
preferences.description: Gap from windows to the screen edge

preferences.name: sidebar
preferences.title: Default Sidebar App
preferences.description: Opened and pinned to the screen by Toggle Sidebar

commands.name: auto-tile
commands.title: Auto Tile
commands.description: Arrange every window on every display in an even grid. Use Cycle Tile Layout to change the grid's shape.

commands.name: toggle-sidebar
commands.title: Toggle Sidebar
commands.description: Open the window chosen as the Default Sidebar App and pin it full height down the right of the screen. Run it again to unpin. While a sidebar is pinned, every other command arranges the remaining windows beside it.

commands.name: make-sidebar
commands.title: Make Sidebar
commands.description: Pin the focused window full height down the right of the screen, whatever app it is. It stays the sidebar until you unpin it with Toggle Sidebar.

commands.name: pivot
commands.title: Cycle Tile Layout
commands.description: Change the shape of Auto Tile. Each run steps to the next shape: all windows side by side, two small above one large, then two small beside one large.

commands.name: smart-arrange
commands.title: Smart Arrange
commands.description: Arrange windows by what each app is for. The focused window leads your largest display with related work beside it. Chat, mail and music go to your other display.

commands.name: master-left
commands.title: Master Left
commands.description: Make the focused window the master on the left, with every other window stacked on the right.

commands.name: master-right
commands.title: Master Right
commands.description: Make the focused window the master on the right, with every other window stacked on the left.

commands.name: master-center
commands.title: Master Center
commands.description: Make the focused window the master in the middle, with the other windows stacked on both sides. Best on wide displays.

commands.name: cycle-master
commands.title: Cycle Master Layout
commands.description: Move the master to its next position. Each run steps round: left, then right, then center.

commands.name: grow-master
commands.title: Make Master Larger
commands.description: Give the master window 5% more of the screen. The stacked windows shrink to make room.

commands.name: shrink-master
commands.title: Make Master Smaller
commands.description: Give the master window 5% less of the screen. The stacked windows grow to fill the space.

commands.name: swap-with-master
commands.title: Swap with Master
commands.description: Make the focused window the master. It trades places with the current master.

commands.name: swap-next
commands.title: Swap with Next Window
commands.description: Trade places between the focused window and the next one in the layout. With two windows, they simply swap.

commands.name: rotate
commands.title: Rotate Windows Clockwise
commands.description: Move every window one position clockwise in the current layout. A pinned sidebar stays where it is.

commands.name: rotate-backwards
commands.title: Rotate Windows Counterclockwise
commands.description: Move every window one position counterclockwise in the current layout. A pinned sidebar stays where it is.

commands.name: swap-displays
commands.title: Swap Displays
commands.description: Send every window to your other display and tile it there. With more than two displays, each display's windows move to the next one.

commands.name: distribute-displays
commands.title: Distribute Across Displays
commands.description: Spread windows over all your displays in proportion to their size, so no display is crowded while another sits empty.

commands.name: move-others
commands.title: Move Others to Next Display
commands.description: Keep only the focused window on this display. Every other window here moves to your next display.

commands.name: move-all
commands.title: Move All to This Display
commands.description: Bring every window from your other displays to the one you are working on.

commands.name: toggle-menu-bar-visibility
commands.title: Toggle Menu Bar Visibility
commands.description: Hide or show the macOS menu bar, to give windows the full height of the screen.

tools.name: get-windows
tools.title: Get Windows
tools.description: List every display and every open window on the current desktop, with its app, title, display and frame.

tools.name: arrange-windows
tools.title: Arrange Windows
tools.description: Move windows onto chosen displays in a chosen order and tile each display with a chosen layout.

ai.instructions:
You arrange the user's open windows so they suit what the user is doing.
Always call get-windows first, then call arrange-windows once with a plan for every display.
Work out the task from the apps, window titles and each window's role (work, reference, comms or background). Put the window the user is working in (usually the focused one, or the editor, document or design tool) first on the largest display, and use a master layout when one window clearly matters most.
Keep related windows together on one display, such as an editor with its terminal and browser preview.
Put supporting windows such as chat, music, mail, notes and settings on the smaller display, or last in the order.
A display fits about three windows side by side when it is under 1600 points wide, and about six when it is wider. Do not give a display more than that unless there is nowhere else to put them.
Use auto-tile when the windows matter equally. Use master-center only on displays wider than 2000 points.
After arranging, say in one or two sentences what you put where and why. Do not list frames or ids.
